what_its_for: Duvelisib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with certain types of blood cancers. It is used for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) in patients who have already tried at least 2 other treatments. It is also used for a type of lymphoma called follicular lymphoma (FL) in patients who have already tried at least 2 other treatments. Duvelisib works by blocking certain proteins that help cancer cells grow and survive.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsule. Try to take it at the same times every day. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose — just wait and take your next scheduled dose.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 25 mg taken by mouth twice a day (about 12 hours apart), every day in 28-day cycles. Your doctor may lower your dose or ask you to take a break from the medicine if you have side effects. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed — do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since your scheduled time, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take 2 doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store duvelisib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the capsules in their original bottle with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and light. Store it safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of leftover capsules.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges, and starfruit while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) as it can make duvelisib less effective. Avoid people who are sick or have infections, since this medicine can weaken your immune system. Avoid live vaccines (such as flu nasal spray, shingles vaccine Zostavax, or MMR) unless your doctor says it is safe. Tell all your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, and supplement you take, as many drugs can interact with duvelisib.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fever, chills, or signs of infection (this could be a serious lung, gut, or skin infection); new or worsening cough, trouble breathing, or chest pain; severe diarrhea or stomach pain (more than 4 loose stools a day); blood in your stool or black tarry stools; yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe nausea and vomiting (signs of liver problems); a new skin rash or blistering of the skin; swollen, painful joints; unusual tiredness or weakness; or signs of low blood counts such as easy bruising, unusual bleeding, pale skin, or feeling very tired.
when_it_works: Duvelisib starts working in your body right away, but it may take several weeks to months before you and your doctor notice improvement in your condition. Your doctor will check your blood regularly and do other tests to see how well the medicine is working. Do not stop taking duvelisib without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Duvelisib can harm an unborn baby. Do not become pregnant while taking this medicine. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Male patients with female partners who can become pregnant should also use birth control during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 1 month after the last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have liver problems. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild to moderate kidney problems, but tell your doctor if you have kidney disease. Older adults (65 and older): Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, especially infections and diarrhea — your doctor will monitor you closely.
